investigation: BASS-II — Material Ignition and Suppression Test (MIST)

material: Black and clear PMMA rods, diameters 0.25, 0.375 and 0.5 in
finding: The poster reports flame-spread rates tending to decrease with increasing rod diameter in both gravity conditions; 1-g rates were higher in its comparison. In microgravity, average rates tended to increase with oxygen concentration.

investigation: BASS-II — Spacecraft Materials Microgravity Research on Flammability
source_locator: PDF slide 18 (PDF page 18), 'Spacecraft Materials Microgravity Research on Flammability: Status'
material: PMMA rod, 0.25 in diameter
finding: The poster reports steady flame spread for the quarter-inch PMMA rod at 13.6% oxygen in microgravity, compared with a 1-g blowoff limit at 16% oxygen.
fire_safety_relevance: 24 PMMA rods burned (overall set); oxygen margin of safety reported as -2.4 percentage points O2 for this comparison.
limitations: Comparison is specific to the reported rod and flow geometry; 13.6% is not a universal PMMA oxygen ignition threshold, and no numerical airflow is provided for this comparison.
